Foundations / PAPER 02

The Omnicorp charter

A design question: what could an organisation become if AI were part of its foundations, and continual development were its purpose?

ŁUKASZ STOCKI & ARGOPUBLIC EDITION / 05 NOV 20263 MIN READ
IN THIS PAPER

EXPLORE THE LIBRARY ↗
WORKING PAPER · DESIGN & ANALYSIS
01

The question we are exploring

Omnicorp begins with a question about organisation. If AI can contribute directly to research, judgment and execution, how should a company be designed around that possibility? Adding an assistant to an existing process is one answer. Reconsidering the process, its responsibilities and its feedback is a more demanding one.

The ambition is broad, but its cornerstone is specific: continually improve the organisation’s ability to understand, learn and act. Products and work in the world give that development resources, constraints and consequences. They help reveal whether a new capability is useful beyond the environment in which it was created.

02

The organisation is part of the invention

The charter uses electrification as a historical analogy. A new source of power did not automatically produce a better factory. Layout, machinery, workflow and skills had to change together. The analogy suggests that the productive use of AI will also require complementary changes in how work is arranged.

This is a design argument, not a prediction that history will repeat on a particular schedule. A capable model alone does not supply a trustworthy organisation. Clear ownership, usable information, appropriate tools, independent evaluation and human accountability all shape what the technology can accomplish.

03

A purpose with contact with reality

Continual development does not mean treating every change as progress. A better process should improve a relevant outcome, retain valuable capabilities and remain answerable to its intended purpose. The organisation needs ways to distinguish a useful advance from novelty, a persuasive explanation or a result that only works on familiar examples.

Useful activity provides that contact with reality. Building something people need creates feedback that internal demonstrations cannot supply. The commercial and practical dimensions therefore belong inside the design, while remaining means of sustaining the larger purpose rather than its complete definition.

04

A blueprint with different confidence levels

The nearer questions concern software, research, coordination and repeatable workflows. These allow relatively short feedback cycles and bounded experiments. The further questions concern physical operations, infrastructure and organisations spanning many domains. Those involve additional constraints and much greater uncertainty.

Omnicorp keeps both horizons in view without treating them as equally established. A design for an agent team is not evidence that the team will work reliably. A path toward a physical industry is not proof of permission, engineering feasibility or operational readiness. Each extension needs evidence appropriate to its consequences.

05

How to read these notes

These public documents share an evolving body of thinking: the architecture, the growth path, the proposed workforce and the questions behind continual development. They are design notes, not a report that the complete organisation already exists.

The invitation is to examine the structure of the idea. Which parts would make learning cumulative? Which decisions need human judgment? What would show that a proposed system can act more effectively while preserving continuity and trust? Those questions matter more than an impressive diagram.

THE NEXT QUESTIONS

What remains open.

  • What would count as useful cumulative development?
  • Which organisational complements must change together?
  • Where does the analogy with earlier technologies stop being useful?

ABOUT THIS EDITION

Adapted from the Omnicorp working document “00 CHARTER”. This is an edited public essay, not a verbatim release of internal notes. The founding purpose is continual development of the organisation’s ability to understand and act; commercial and physical work sustain and ground it.
